title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BENNY'S BIG TYPO
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Benny Archuleta, a sign painter from Albuquerque, New Mexico.
One day, he painted one word wrong. Twelve feet tall.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE TYPO
segments.quote: A sense of humor is just common sense, dancing.
segments.author: Clive James
lines: Tía Rosa's new restaurant sign said: Best Enchiladas in Albequerque.
He misspelled his own hometown. The picture went everywhere.
Benny wanted to hide. Then his wife Carmen read him a line from the writer Clive James:
A sense of humor is just common sense, dancing.
So Benny posted his own picture, under the sign, holding a dictionary upside down. Now the city laughed with him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE DARE
segments.quote: He who is not courageous enough to take risks will accomplish nothing in life.
segments.author: Muhammad Ali
lines: Then a flyer came. The Grown-Up Spelling Bee at the Elks Lodge, for the food bank.
Benny said, Me? I'm the Albequerque guy.
Carmen pointed at his old boxing poster, with a line from Muhammad Ali:
He who is not courageous enough to take risks will accomplish nothing in life.
Benny signed up. Spelled his name right. He checked.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE CHAMP
segments.quote: Talent is cheaper than table salt. What separates the talented individual from the successful one is a lot of hard work.
segments.author: Stephen King
lines: The champ, three years running, was Gary Pruitt, the car dealer.
Benny figured Gary was born with it. Then he read the novelist Stephen King:
Talent is cheaper than table salt. What separates the talented individual from the successful one is a lot of hard work.
So Benny painted ten words a night on scrap boards. By March, his garage looked like a dictionary exploded.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE RIVAL
segments.quote: Never ascribe to an opponent motives meaner than your own.
segments.author: J. M. Barrie
lines: At the hardware store, Gary grinned. Good luck, Albequerque.
Benny's face went hot. Then he remembered J. M. Barrie, the Scottish writer who gave us Peter Pan:
Never ascribe to an opponent motives meaner than your own.
Benny had made that same joke first. So he painted Gary a little sign: Good luck to you too. Gary hung it in his office.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE STAGE
segments.quote: Don't think. Thinking is the enemy of creativity.
segments.author: Ray Bradbury
lines: Bee night. Round after round, people sat down.
Then Benny got mischievous. His mind went blank.
He remembered Ray Bradbury, his favorite writer:
Don't think. Thinking is the enemy of creativity.
So he stopped thinking, and painted the letters in the air, like a sign. Correct.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAST WORD
segments.quote: The difference between the almost right word and the right word is really a large matter—'tis the difference between the lightning bug and the lightning.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: Then it was Benny and Gary. Gary missed rhythm. One word to win.
The judge smiled. Your word is Albuquerque. The room howled.
Benny thought of Mark Twain:
The difference between the almost right word and the right word is really a large matter—'tis the difference between the lightning bug and the lightning.
He spelled it slowly, and got it right. On Monday, he fixed Tía Rosa's sign. Gary held the ladder.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Laugh. Take the risk. Do the work. Think kindly. Stop overthinking. Get the word right.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Laugh at your mistakes. Take the risk. Do the work. Think kindly. Stop overthinking. Get the word right.
Me? I once spelled my own name wrong on a check. The bank cashed it anyway.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
